❗️ XRP price forms multi-month falling wedge near $1 support as liquidations mount 

📣 According to data from cryptonews price, XRP price dropped from around $1.07 on June 25 to $1.01 on June 26, extending its year-to-date decline to more than 40%. The decline accelerated as a $10.8 billion crypto options expiry triggered heavy volatility across digital assets and forced a wave of long liquidations.

⚠️ At the same time, sentiment surrounding the XRP ecosystem weakened after decentralized finance protocol Strobe Finance abruptly announced it would shut down operations.

🔖 The daily chart shows XRP trading at the lower edge of a falling wedge that has contained price action for almost a year. The pattern has compressed between descending resistance and gradually declining support, with the token now sitting close to the wedge’s lower boundary near $1.00.

🔗 Momentum indicators remain weak. The MACD has stayed below its signal line with histogram bars still in negative territory, while the Aroon indicator continues to favor sellers after Aroon Down climbed back toward 100 and Aroon Up remained subdued. Together, the indicators suggest bears still control the short-term trend even as XRP price approaches a historically important support zone.

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Head of the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI) Mohammad Eslami has called for accelerating the implementation of a cold plasma-based industrial wastewater treatment project, highlighting the technology’s potential to improve wastewater treatment processes and support environmental protection.

Eslami, who also serves as vice president, visited Kaveh Industrial City and Special Economic Zone, near the northern city of Saveh, on Wednesday to inspect the construction of an industrial wastewater treatment plant based on indigenous cold plasma technology.
​
During the visit, he toured various sections of the project, including the EDR hall, the equalization structure, and the plasma treatment unit, which is designed to process 2,000 cubic meters of industrial wastewater per day. He was briefed on the progress of construction and the latest developments.
​
Emphasizing the importance of developing advanced technologies for environmental protection and water resource management, Eslami described the project as an important step toward the industrial-scale application of cold plasma technology.
​
He also pointed to the technology’s significant potential to enhance wastewater treatment quality, stressing the need for expediting the project’s completion to enable the earliest possible deployment of the homegrown, knowledge-based technology.

🎙 Exclusive | Martyred Iranian Leader’s vision will endure across Muslim world: Lebanese scholar

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The ideas and legacy of the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, will continue to influence the Muslim world, emphasizing the former Leader’s role in promoting Islamic unity, supporting oppressed people, and advancing the discourse of resistance, a Lebanese thinker says.

In an exclusive interview with IRNA, Sheikh Ahmad al-Qattan, head of Lebanon’s Qawluna wal Amal (Our Word and Action) Association, called unity among Muslims a central principle of Ayatollah Khamenei’s thought.
​
He said Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei viewed Islamic unity as both a religious obligation and a source of strength, consistently calling on Muslims to reject division and strengthen bonds of brotherhood.
​
Al-Qattan said Ayatollah Khamenei sought to promote solidarity rather than sectarianism, pointing to his well-known religious ruling prohibiting insults against the Prophet Muhammad’s companions and Sunni religious symbols as an example of His commitment to Muslim unity. He also cited Tehran’s conferences on Islamic unity as practical expressions of that approach.
​
The Lebanese cleric argued that the Muslim world’s greatest need today is greater cooperation based on shared values and resistance to division. He urged Muslims not to align themselves with global Zionism or arrogant powers, stressing the importance of preserving the unity of the Islamic community.
​
According to al-Qattan, Ayatollah Khamenei’s concept of resistance extended far beyond military action. He said resistance also includes intellectual work, education, scientific innovation, social activism, and cultural engagement, allowing individuals to contribute from their own fields.
​
The expert added that the martyred Iranian Leader consistently encouraged support for oppressed people, particularly in Palestine, Al-Quds, Gaza, and Lebanon.
​
Al-Qattan concluded that Ayatollah Khamenei’s assassination was intended to undermine those principles but would instead strengthen their place in the conscience of the Islamic nation.

⚡️ Iran’s envoy urges accountability over Western role in Sardasht chemical attack

📌 London, IRNA – Iran’s ambassador to Germany has called for accountability for Western companies and industrial actors that enabled Saddam Hussein’s regime to carry out the 1987 chemical attack on the Iranian border city of Sardasht by providing him with chemical weapons materials and technology.

Ambassador Majid Nili said in a message posted on X on Wednesday that he had sent a letter to Germany’s “free-thinking people” on the anniversary of the Sardasht chemical attack.
​
“In the letter, I asked, ‘How did some Western companies and industrial actors make the Saddam regime’s access to materials and technology for producing chemical weapons possible, and why were international mechanisms unable to prevent this crime?’” he wrote.
​
Nili said that he had also stressed that to prevent the recurrence of such tragedies, adding, “Holding the perpetrators and suppliers of this crime accountable is a necessity, not a choice.”
​
The ambassador had earlier said that history would not forget not only the direct perpetrators of the attack but also those who supplied the technology and equipment and those who remained silent.
​
On June 28, 1987, Iraq’s Ba’athist regime used internationally prohibited chemical weapons against Sardasht, striking four crowded areas of the city. The attack killed 119 civilians and exposed over 8,000 others to toxic gases, leaving many with lasting injuries. Sardasht is widely regarded as the world’s first city targeted by chemical weapons after the atomic bombing of Hiroshima.

📡 Iran, Belarus seek to expand agricultural cooperation

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s agriculture minister has emphasized the need to expand bilateral cooperation with Belarus in the agricultural sector, increase trade between the two countries, and accelerate the convening of their joint agricultural commission.

According to a press release by Iran’s Agriculture Ministry on Wednesday, Gholamreza Nouri Ghezeljeh met with Belarusian Ambassador to Tehran Dmitry Kaltsov to discuss ways to strengthen bilateral relations in agriculture and related industries.
​
During the meeting, both sides highlighted the significant potential of Iran and Belarus in agricultural production, livestock, and agricultural machinery, stressing the importance of increasing trade and facilitating broader economic cooperation.
​
Key topics included expanding imports and exports of agricultural and livestock products, enhancing cooperation in agricultural machinery, particularly combine harvesters, and exploring new areas of cooperation in the agricultural sector.
​
The two sides also agreed to expedite the convening of the Iran-Belarus Joint Agricultural Cooperation Commission, describing it as an effective mechanism for implementing agreements, removing obstacles, and deepening technical, economic, and trade ties between Tehran and Minsk.
​
They also underscored the importance of continuing consultations and strengthening bilateral cooperation to make better use of their respective capacities in agriculture and food security.
